      "title": "Client-side upload limit is hardcoded to 10MB",
      "body": "The upload validator now uses a constant 10MB limit for every file instead of the type-specific site setting (`max_image_size_kb` or `max_attachment_size_kb`). This makes client-side enforcement inconsistent with admin configuration: files above the configured limit can be submitted, and files below a higher configured limit can be rejected. The too-large alert also reports the wrong limit."

      "title": "413 error message uses a hardcoded limit",

      "severity": "high",
      "category": "security",
      "title": "URL downloads ignore configured upload size limits",
      "body": "API uploads supplied by URL are downloaded with a fixed 10MB cap rather than the configured limit. The subsequent automatic reduction only runs for filenames that look like images, so non-image files, or images that cannot be reduced, may be processed despite lower site limits, and the server will fetch more data than configured."
    },

      "severity": "high",
      "category": "data",
      "title": "Downsizing rewrites the uploaded tempfile in place",
      "body": "The downsize operation passes the same filesystem path as source and destination to external image tools. In-place rewriting of an open tempfile is not safe for ImageMagick or gifsicle; a tool failure or partial write can truncate or corrupt the original uploaded file before it is stored. A separate output file should be used and replaced only after success."
    },

As a result, an animated GIF can be processed with ImageMagick's first-frame-only path and reduced to a static image, silently losing animation even when animation is allowed."
    },

findings.title: Client-side upload limit is hardcoded to 10MB
findings.body: The upload validator now uses a constant 10MB limit for every file instead of the type-specific site setting (`max_image_size_kb` or `max_attachment_size_kb`). This makes client-side enforcement inconsistent with admin configuration: files above the configured limit can be submitted, and files below a higher configured limit can be rejected. The too-large alert also reports the wrong limit.

findings.title: 413 error message uses a hardcoded limit
findings.body: When a 413 response is received, the message is generated with a fixed 10MB maximum. This is incorrect for attachments and for sites where the configured upload limit differs from 10MB.

findings.title: URL downloads ignore configured upload size limits
findings.body: API uploads supplied by URL are downloaded with a fixed 10MB cap rather than the configured limit. The subsequent automatic reduction only runs for filenames that look like images, so non-image files, or images that cannot be reduced, may be processed despite lower site limits, and the server will fetch more data than configured.

findings.title: Downsizing rewrites the uploaded tempfile in place
findings.body: The downsize operation passes the same filesystem path as source and destination to external image tools. In-place rewriting of an open tempfile is not safe for ImageMagick or gifsicle; a tool failure or partial write can truncate or corrupt the original uploaded file before it is stored. A separate output file should be used and replaced only after success.

findings.title: Animated GIFs can be silently flattened
findings.body: Animated GIF handling is selected by checking whether the source path ends in .gif, but the tempfile path used for uploads generally does not include the original extension. As a result, an animated GIF can be processed with ImageMagick's first-frame-only path and reduced to a static image, silently losing animation even when animation is allowed.

findings.title: Failed downsize operations are ignored
findings.body: `OptimizedImage.downsize` returns false if conversion or optimization fails, but this return value is ignored. The loop can retry a failing conversion five times and then continue to create an upload from the unchanged or corrupted tempfile instead of returning a clear error.

findings.title: Upload proceeds without verifying final image size
findings.body: After at most five 80% reductions, the code calls `Upload.create_for` without confirming that the file is now within `max_image_size_kb`. If downsizing cannot reach the limit, the request either depends on downstream validation or stores an oversized image, and the user does not get a specific failure for the automatic downsizing step.

findings.title: Duplicate `downsize` definition silently overwrites previous method
findings.body: Ruby does not support method overloading. This second definition of `self.downsize` replaces the previous width/height version. Existing callers that pass `max_width` and `max_height` will now have `max_height` treated as the options argument, or receive an ArgumentError for five arguments, breaking the previous API.

findings.title: No tests for automatic downsizing behavior
findings.body: No tests were added for the new automatic downsizing flow. The behavior includes conditional size checks, external command failure handling, animation preservation, and in-place tempfile mutation, all of which are likely to regress without controller and model specs.
